16.0.s.en: (1) Paul's greetings to the believers in Rome

16.0.0.en: "Phebe": a name meaning radiant. She was a deaconess in the church of Cenchrea, which is the port of the city of Corinth (in present-day Greece). It appears that Phebe was wealthy and loved to give, and she spent her money to serve many, including Paul himself, so he asks them to appreciate her and help her to complete her service. And he places Phebe at the head of the list of those to whom he sends greetings, before the men, because she was distinguished above all in her love and service. There is no distinction between man and woman before God except in love.

16.1.0.en: "Who have for my life laid down their own necks": Paul faced severe persecutions that threatened his life, and this couple defended him and exposed themselves to death for Paul's sake. Perhaps this was in hosting him or accompanying him.

16.1.1.en: "All the churches of the Gentiles": they helped Paul in his ministry to the Gentiles in many lands, so they deserved to be thanked by them.

16.1.2.en: Note here the mention of the wife Priscilla before her husband Aquila, because she was more zealous for the ministry. They were Jews who were expelled with the Jews from Rome, so they went to Corinth and received Paul in their house, and helped him in his ministry to the Gentiles, so the churches of the Gentiles such as Rome ought to honor them.

16.2.0.en: Because of the persecution of the Christians in the apostolic age, they were compelled to hold the Liturgies and prayers in houses, being unable to build church buildings. It appears that the house of Aquila and Priscilla was a center where the Liturgies were held, so Paul sent his greeting to the company of believers who attend this church that is held in their house.

16.2.1.en: Paul continues his discourse and greets Epaenetus, who was the first to believe in the region of Achaia, in present-day Greece.

16.3.0.en: "Mary": a Jewish woman who rendered many services to the Church, and the Apostle Paul, by his greeting to her, shows his appreciation of her deeds.

16.4.0.en: "Andronicus and Junia": two Jews who believed in Christ before Paul, and labored in the ministry until they were imprisoned, and bore many tribulations. They are related to Paul by kinship.

16.4.1.en: "My fellowprisoners": they were imprisoned with Paul during his preaching, and the time or place of this imprisonment is not mentioned because Paul was imprisoned many times (2 Cor 6:5). "Of note among the apostles": known for their love and distinguished service.

16.5.0.en: "Amplias": one of the well-known believers in Rome. With overflowing feelings Paul describes him as his beloved.

16.6.0.en: "Urbane": one of the well-known servants, and he describes him as a helper in Christ, that is, one who does not seek his own glory but the spreading of the name of Christ.

16.6.1.en: "Stachys": one of the believers beloved to Paul.

16.7.1.en: "Aristobulus": a well-known wealthy person, but a pagan, and therefore Paul did not greet him. "Them which are of Aristobulus' household": probably his slaves or relatives who had become Christians.

16.8.0.en: "Herodion": a Jew, so he calls him my kinsman, and there may be a close or distant kinship between them. "Narcissus": he was a slave who believed and was freed, then was martyred for the name of Christ, and his household, that is, his relatives, continued their strong spiritual life with God, so the Apostle Paul sends them greetings and encouragement and praises them because their life is connected with God.

16.9.0.en: "Tryphena and Tryphosa": two maidservants who believed in Christ and served Him. As for Persis, she is an old woman who served the Lord. He calls her the beloved because of her giving and her abundant love.

16.10.0.en: "Rufus": the son of Simon the Cyrenian, and his mother showed care for the Apostle Paul, so he calls her his mother.

16.11.0.en: Paul mentions a group of names of Christians, some of whom were slaves and were freed, and there was with them a company of Christians. It appears that groups of Christians had formed in various parts of Rome, each group worshiping God in a strong Christian life.

16.12.0.en: Philologus and Julia, husband and wife, and their children Nereus and his sister Olympas: this family was part of another Christian company in Rome, to whom Paul sent greetings and love.

16.13.0.en: He sends them greetings and love in the form of the apostolic kiss, as the deacon calls out in the Liturgy, saying, "Greet one another." This means forgiveness and love so that we may be prepared for Christ to dwell in us. And the churches of the Gentiles send greetings to the Church in Rome, which is the capital of the empire.

16.13.1.en: How beautiful is the bond between the members of one Church, and between the different churches. Offer your love to all your fellow believers, for love creates a path of cooperation and encourages holding fast to Christ amid the tribulations of life.

16.14.0.en: "Divisions": that is, thoughts outside the one true faith that they learned from the apostolic teachings.

16.14.1.en: "Offences": that is, one does right things but causes others to fall into sins, since they understand the action in a wrong way and doubt and so are kept away from God.

16.14.2.en: St. Paul asks the believers to watch, as guards, with caution anyone who tries to create divisions or offences in the Church, so that they may preserve the level of love and the one unity in the Church.

16.15.0.en: "Their own belly": their personal gains and private aims.

16.15.2.en: Why should we mark them? Because they are not obvious. They slip into houses and into the midst of the Church, claiming to be her children, and they speak general Christian words, sweet and good, with outward holiness and deceptive kindness, so many are deceived by them and follow them, and it is not long before they inject their poisons like vipers, and kill many spiritually among the peaceable and kind who love everyone and suspect no one. Their aim in this is material gain, since houses open their doors to them with food, drink, hospitality, money and fame, and they certainly have no connection with the service of Jesus Christ.

16.16.0.en: You are famous for the obedience that I love in you, but let this virtue be only for the one who deserves obedience, that is, the Church, and not for the innovators who think you are easy prey for them. Therefore even the good, that is, obedience, should be with wisdom and discernment, but as for evil, be simple in it, that is, as though you were children who do not know it and do not deal with it or experience it.

16.16.1.en: Beloved, do not open your ear or your house to anyone who claims to be from the Church, but verify his identity with great care.

16.17.0.en: So by our unity, our fighting against heresies and our love, we will overcome Satan and he will be crushed, because our Lord Jesus Christ fights for us, and Satan falls defeated under our feet, those that strive and labor, not the lazy feet. And in this Christ overcomes Satan through us.

16.17.1.en: Look, beloved, at the power of God, who holds your right hand to fight the devil, so do not fear his wars and evil temptations, because the One who is with you is your victorious God, who has already crushed Satan in the battle of the Cross.

16.18.0.en: Out of St. Paul's love and humility, he did not want to be the only one with love for them, so he pointed to others who have the same love for the Church of Rome, as though he were saying that without them he could not have completed my epistle. These who are mentioned are the servants accompanying Paul. Among them is Timotheus, the closest of Paul's disciples to his heart, to whom he wrote two epistles. And Lucius is a person other than Luke the Evangelist, while Jason was Paul's host when he preached in Thessalonica, and Sosipater is probably the one mentioned in (Acts 20:4), and these are relatives of Paul.

16.19.0.en: "Tertius": the writer of the epistle. Paul did not write by himself because of the illness of his eyes. Tertius also sends his greeting to the believers in the Church of Rome.

16.20.0.en: "Gaius": the host of St. Paul while he wrote the epistle, and he opened his house to the believers. "Erastus": who worked as the one in charge of the state's storehouses in Corinth.

16.20.1.en: "Quartus": perhaps he had no great position in society, but he was as a brother to St. Paul, for he values every person however simple.

16.20.2.en: Therefore, beloved, the servant must not be the only star beloved to those he serves, but he should point to the others who labored with him or served with him. So encourage and praise everyone who shares with you in the ministry, appreciating every labor, even if it is small.

16.21.0.en: Paul prays for the people of the Church of Rome that the grace of Christ may accompany them and dwell in them, so that they may be able to fulfill the commandments of his epistle, and understand and stand firm in its teachings.

16.22.0.en: "The mystery": the acceptance of the Gentiles into the faith.

16.22.1.en: "Eternal times": in the thought of God before the foundation of the world.

16.22.2.en: God is able to establish the Gospel thought that I taught you, which is that Christ Jesus accepts the Gentiles into His Church together with their brothers the Jews. This thought was a mystery, that is, not accepted or understood among the Jews at that time, but God has now revealed it to us in the New Testament, so that I may preach to the Gentiles that they may have a share in the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

16.23.0.en: The prophets of the Old Testament had already prophesied of the entering of the Gentiles, but the Jews did not understand that in the past. Now it has become known, evident and understood by all. The entering of the Gentiles into faith is not according to Paul's personal thought, but because it has been God's command from eternity that the Gentiles would obey the faith.

16.24.0.en: Here is the sum of the epistle: that our wise and loving God allowed the entering of the Gentiles by means of the atoning work of Christ. To Him be the glory, for He arranged for us the plan of salvation. Amen.

16.24.1.en: "By Phebe": either she took part in writing a portion of the epistle with Tertius (v. 22), or she delivered this epistle by her own hand.

16.24.2.en: The love of God seeks the salvation of all, so do not despise anyone or be annoyed with him, for he may be a vessel that God will fill at the right time, even if this seems a mystery hidden from people for many years. So pray, and encourage everyone to be bound to God.
